title: Cuemath & Aakash Franchise Alternative for Tutors (2026)
description: For tutors weighing a Cuemath or Aakash franchise against their own brand: what each publishes today, what to read in your agreement, and costs checked 24 Oct 2026.
og_description: Neither Cuemath nor Aakash publishes current franchise terms. Here is what they do publish, the clauses to read in your own agreement, and what running your own coaching brand costs, with sources dated.
h1: Cuemath and Aakash Franchise Alternative for Tutors: Franchise vs Your Own Brand (2026)
dek: A fair look at the choice between a coaching franchise and a brand of your own: what Cuemath and Aakash publish today, the clauses to read in your agreement, and what an independent academy costs. Every source is linked and dated.
cover_alt: Leaving a coaching franchise: Cuemath, Aakash and your own brand compared, with official sources checked on 24 Oct 2026
audience: Tutors and centre operators in India who run, or are considering, a Cuemath or Aakash franchise and want to compare it with an independent coaching brand
intro: The alternative to a Cuemath or Aakash franchise is a coaching brand under your own name, with your own website, app, courses and fees, started only when your franchise agreement allows it. For some tutors, staying in the franchise is still the better choice; for others, owning the brand matters more. Your agreement decides what you can do and when.

We are AllCoaching, so read this knowing who wrote it. Every fact about another company comes from its own website, linked and dated. This guide is not legal or financial advice: we cannot read your contract, so we tell you which clauses to read and when to ask a lawyer.

We checked both companies on 24 Oct 2026. Neither publishes current franchise terms. Aakash's only franchise page we found is a 2019 application form that is marked closed. Cuemath now presents online maths tutoring mainly for US students and publishes no tutor or franchise programme. So any claim you read about their current franchise fees, revenue share or territory rules should be checked with them directly.
takeaways: Aakash publishes no current franchise terms. Its only franchise page found is a 2019 form, marked closed, with a ₹2,000 application fee and a last date of 20 April 2019 (checked 24 Oct 2026).
Cuemath publishes no tutor or franchise programme; its site now presents maths tutoring and test prep mainly for US students (checked 24 Oct 2026).

Your franchise agreement decides what you can do, including exit notice, non-compete, territory, and who owns student records and material. Read it before any move, and ask a lawyer if a clause is unclear.
Your own brand means your name, your fees and your student list, and it also means finding students yourself.
AllCoaching starts at ₹6,999 a year plus 10% of sales (Growth ₹12,999 + 7.5%, Pro ₹24,999 + 5%), GST extra, with a 14-day free trial and no card needed.
Classplus lists ₹29,999 for 1 year and Learnyst ₹10,000 a year + 10% (Launcher); on published prices AllCoaching costs less than Classplus up to ₹2.3 lakh of sales a year.
Rebuild study material in your own words rather than reusing franchise material, unless your agreement clearly allows it.

sections.h2: The short answer: stay, or build your own brand when your agreement allows
sections.html:
A franchise tutor has two honest options: stay in the franchise while it works for you, or build a coaching brand of your own when your agreement allows. Which one fits depends on your contract, your local reputation and how much of the marketing you want to own.

{{fig:verdict|Franchise or own brand, by situation: agreement still working, stay for now; own name on website and app, AllCoaching; JEE or NEET centre built on mock tests, Learnyst; flat-price app at higher sales, Classplus|Pick the row that sounds like you. The rest of this guide explains each choice.}}

If you are mid-agreement, the useful work now is preparation: read the agreement, note the dates, and plan the academy you will open when you are free to.

sections.h2: Why franchise tutors consider their own brand
sections.html:
A franchise can give a new tutor a known name and a ready structure, and that has real value. Tutors start comparing when their own reputation has grown, when the terms no longer suit them, or when they want to set their own fees and courses.

What Aakash publishes today

Aakash calls itself "India's Top Coaching Institute" with "36+ Years of Legacy", teaching NEET, JEE, Olympiads and foundation classes.[1] The only franchise page we found is an old application form, marked closed, with a ₹2,000 application fee and a last date of 20 April 2019.[2] It shows no current franchise fee, revenue share or territory rules. If you run an Aakash centre, your signed agreement is the only reliable source.

What Cuemath publishes today

Cuemath calls itself "The Math Expert", and its site now presents online maths tutoring and test prep (such as SAT and AMC 8) mainly for a US audience.[3] Its /teach page now shows its blog, not a tutor or franchise programme.[4] If you work with Cuemath, ask it in writing for your current terms.

{{q:Can I start my own brand while I still run a franchise centre?|It depends entirely on your agreement. Many agreements have clauses on exclusivity, non-compete and territory that apply during the agreement and sometimes after it. Read them first, and ask a lawyer who handles franchise agreements if anything is unclear. Building your academy in private and launching later is different from selling to students now.}}

What changes with your own brand

With your own academy, families see your name, you set the fees and batches, and the student list is yours. You also take on what the brand did for you, mainly marketing. That trade is the real decision.

{{fig:before-after|Before and after for a franchise tutor: questions about whose name, student list, fees and material, compared with one academy login with your own website, app, live classes, tests and checkout|Owning the brand means owning the marketing too. Plan for both.}}

sections.h2: What to read in your franchise agreement first
sections.html:
Before you plan anything, read your franchise agreement end to end. These are the clauses that usually decide what you can do and when. We cannot interpret your contract; if any clause is unclear, ask a lawyer.

  1. Term, renewal and exit notice: when the agreement ends, whether it renews on its own, and how much notice you must give.
  2. Non-compete and exclusivity: whether you may teach or run a coaching business outside the franchise, during and after the agreement.
  3. Territory: any area where you may not operate, and for how long.
  4. Students and leads: who owns the student list, enquiries and contact details, and whether you may contact them later.
  5. Material and name: who owns the curriculum, workbooks, tests and recordings, and what must be returned or stop being used.
  6. Money on exit: any fees, deposits or dues that apply when you leave.

Write down the dates and the answers. They tell you whether you can launch now, at renewal, or after a waiting period.

2. Stay with your franchise (Aakash, Cuemath or another)

Good at
A known name and an existing structure. Aakash describes itself as "India's Top Coaching Institute"; Cuemath as "The Math Expert".[1][3]
Published terms
Not listed on either website (checked 24 Oct 2026). Aakash's only franchise page is a closed 2019 form with a ₹2,000 application fee.[2]
Check
Your own agreement: fees, renewal, exit notice and non-compete. Ask the franchisor for current terms in writing.
Best for
Tutors for whom the brand's name and leads are still worth what the agreement costs.

3. Learnyst

Good at
Courses, mock tests and live classes with content protection and test series; it offers the "Features required to market and sell your content online across globe".[6]
Published price
Launcher ₹10,000/yr + 10% of sales; Professional ₹8,999/month (₹8,099/month billed annually) with 0% transaction fees; higher plans up to ₹49,999/month; taxes extra.
Check
Its page says apps are published under Learnyst's developer account; a branded Android app starts from Premium (₹14,999/month).
Best for
JEE and NEET centres where mock tests are the main product.

4. Classplus

Good at
A branded teaching app and website; its page says "Get your own brand's teaching app, create your own website & sell courses".[5]
Published price
₹29,999 for 1 year or ₹39,999 for 2 years (checked 24 Oct 2026).
Free trial
Not mentioned on the pricing page.
Check
GST, any fee on sales and the renewal price are not stated; the plan cards list an Android app but not an iOS app.
Best for
Established centres selling above about ₹2.3 lakh a year that want a flat yearly price.

sections.h2: How to move from a franchise to your own brand
sections.html:
The careful way to move is in order: agreement first, academy second, launch last. Nothing in these steps replaces your agreement or advice from a lawyer.

{{fig:switch|Four steps from a franchise to your own brand: read your agreement, build your academy, write your own material, launch when allowed|Launch only when your agreement allows it.}} {{steps}}

If you also move students from another coaching app, the checklist in how to switch coaching apps without losing students shows how to run both side by side.

items: Read your agreement and note the dates
Find the exit notice, renewal date, non-compete, territory and ownership clauses, and ask a lawyer about anything unclear.
Build your academy in the trial
Start the 14-day trial, add your logo and colours, connect your own domain and set up your courses.
Write your material in your own words
Prepare notes, tests and recordings yourself instead of reusing franchise material, unless your agreement clearly allows it.
Open admissions on your own website and app, and announce your new academy on YouTube, Instagram and WhatsApp.

faq: Which platform should a Cuemath or Aakash franchise tutor use to start an independent brand?

Use a platform that gives you your own website and app under your name, once your agreement allows it. AllCoaching offers this from ₹6,999 a year plus a fee on sales, with a 14-day free trial. Learnyst suits test-heavy centres and Classplus lists a flat ₹29,999 a year.
What do I own when I leave a coaching franchise?

Your franchise agreement decides that. Read the clauses on students and leads, material, name and exit before you plan anything, and ask a lawyer if a clause is unclear. Your subject knowledge and teaching skill are yours; what you may take beyond that depends on the contract.
Does Aakash publish its franchise terms?
No current terms were found on 24 Oct 2026. Aakash's only franchise page is a 2019 application form marked closed, with a ₹2,000 application fee and a last date of 20 April 2019.
Does Cuemath publish a tutor or franchise programme?

No. On 24 Oct 2026 Cuemath's site presented maths tutoring mainly for US students, and its /teach page showed its blog rather than a tutor or franchise programme. Ask Cuemath directly for current terms.
Can I legally start my own brand while running a franchise centre?

It depends on your agreement, which may have exclusivity, non-compete or territory clauses. We cannot interpret your contract; read it and ask a lawyer who handles franchise agreements before you sell to students under your own name.
Will I lose my students when I leave a franchise?
That depends on your agreement and on how families know you. Check who owns the student list and whether you may contact them, then launch your own academy only in the way your agreement allows.
What does it cost to run an independent coaching brand on AllCoaching?
Starter is ₹6,999 a year plus 10% of sales, Growth ₹12,999 plus 7.5% and Pro ₹24,999 plus 5%, GST extra. Every plan includes your own domain, your own Android and iOS app and unlimited live classes.
How long does it take to launch my own coaching app?
You can set up the academy, connect your domain and upload a first course during the 14-day trial. Writing your own study material usually takes longer than the setup, so start it early.
